text:
incident-bot: Pager: High error rate (502/504) observed on api-gateway-prod in us-east-1. Threshold crossed: 12m, aggregated 18% 5xx. Escalation level: P1.

alice_oncall: grabbing this — oncall for api-gateway. pulling dashboards now.

carla_sre: I see a sharp fanout increase from the edge to backend pool, connection pool saturation on svc-auth-proxy (conn_waits rising).

ben_svc: confirmed from the service side — we deployed a small routing tweak 10m ago that increased health-check concurrency. rolling back now.

alice_oncall: can you paste the deploy id? will correlate with traces.

ben_svc: deploy: deploy-2026-03-17-11:02 (canary). rollback started: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/auth-proxy -n prod`

dave_support: we already got 3 customers reporting failed sign-ins — CS ticket numbers in incident thread #5421.

carla_sre: stackdriver snapshot: `svc-auth-proxy->pool_size: 200 -> conn_waiters: 180 -> 502s` TL;DR: clients hit max pools, connections queued and upstream times out.

alice_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) reduce fanout at gateway (rate-limit health checks), 2) open circuit for auth-proxy to route to standby, 3) rollback config (ben), 4) temporary pool bump. Any objections?

eve_infra: I can patch the gateway route config to limit concurrent health checks to 5 per node. Doing dry-run now: `redwood-gwctl patch route health-checks --concurrency=5 --env=prod`

ben_svc: rollback completed on canary and promoted to stable rollback. rollback finished ~2m ago.

alice_oncall: applying gw patch now (eve), also enabling circuit-breaker for auth-proxy in gw: `redwood-gwctl circuit open --service=auth-proxy --threshold=0.2`

eve_infra: gw patch applied. I see the health-check fanout dropping in the next sample.

carla_sre: after gw changes, conn_waiters dropped to 20, 502 rate falling to ~4%. Good signal.

frank_network: flagged possible SYN backlog on LB nodes earlier — we saw increased TCP CLOSE_WAIT counts, might be contributing to timeouts. Network team will keep an eye.

alice_oncall: temporary pool bump requested to auth-proxy: ben, can you increase connection pool to 300 while we stabilize?

ben_svc: bump applied: pool_size=300. Observability shows reduced queuing.

dave_support: telling CS this is mitigated and we're seeing recovery; asking for grace period before closing tickets.

carla_sre: runbook actions logged. Root-cause hypothesis: health-check concurrency regression in the routing tweak caused backend pool exhaustion + LB SYN backlog amplification -> 502/504 spike.

alice_oncall: next steps: - FR (postmortem) assigned to ben_svc + carla_sre - network follow-up (frank_network) for SYN backlog - consider stronger pre-deploy load-sim checks for routing changes - keep pool bump until FR complete.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: error rate returned to baseline (<1%) at 6032110200. Pager closed.

alice_oncall: thanks all — handing off to oncall-followup. If anyone observes a relapse ping this thread. :thumbsup:

ben_svc: will draft mitigation timeline and feature revert details.

frank_network: I'll capture LB metrics and any kernel-level socket issues and attach to the FR.

carla_sre: adding links: dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/boards/ingress/errors?from=6032109600, traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/6032109999

dave_support: leaving a note for CS: "Temporary rollback & connection pool increase mitigated customer impact; tickets staying open until FR finishes."

alice_oncall: closing command room at 6032110300. Good job team.
